slides.title: Browser Session
slides.subtitle: Join the agent's own browser to its Session with a one-time code the agent authorizes
slides.notes: PAP can carry one Session across APIs, conversations and the company's website. This example shows how the browser the agent controls joins the Session the agent already has: through a form on the company's browser-session page, a one-time code, and a request of the agent's own that authorizes the code.

slides.title: Why a Browser Session
slides.statement: One Session, on the **API** and on the **website**: the same user, the same sign-in, the same scopes.
slides.notes: Sometimes the agent needs a company web page. Instead of signing in again, the browser joins the Session the agent already holds, signed in or out.

slides.title: Who takes part
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR M["Model"] subgraph HOST["Your host, trusted"] direction TB A["Personal agent"] -- "read the code" --> B["Agent's own browser
not the user's"] end subgraph CO["Company"] direction TB E["Browser-session endpoint
form, authorize, cookie"] -- "code used once" --> R[("Join codes")] end HOST -- "GET, /authorize, then the form" --> CO HOST -. "statuses, booleans" .-> M
slides.caption: The code comes from the company's page in the agent's own browser; the model gets statuses and yes-or-no evidence.
slides.notes: Inside the host, the personal agent has its own browser, not the user's ordinary browser, load the company's browser-session endpoint, the one discovery advertised. The page holds a one-time code. The host reads it from that page alone and sends it to the endpoint's /authorize URL, with the Session header and the access token if signed in. The browser then posts the code back; the company checks it and answers 303 with its own cookie for the Session. Off to the side, the model receives statuses and yes-or-no evidence, never the code, the Session JWT or the cookie.

slides.title: Joining the Session

items.title: Load
items.detail: GET the endpoint: a form with a one-time code

items.title: Tie
items.detail: A __Host- SameSite=Strict cookie binds code to browser

items.title: Authorize
items.detail: POST `{endpoint}/authorize`: code, Session header, access token if signed in

items.title: Submit
items.detail: The browser posts the code alone

slides.notes: The browser loads the endpoint with a GET as a top-level navigation. The page is a form with a hidden code of at least 128 random bits, valid for 60 seconds at most; a __Host- cookie, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, ties the code to this browser. The agent authorizes the code at {endpoint}/authorize, as JSON, with the Session header and, if signed in, the access token. The company answers 204. The browser then submits the form; the company answers 303 with its own cookie for the Session. The access token never passes through the browser.

slides.title: Agent responsibilities
items: Join only at the advertised HTTPS `web.browser_session_endpoint`
Read the code from the page **its own browser** loaded, nowhere else
Authorize with the Session header of the Session the browser joins
Add the access token when the website should act signed in
Read and authorize in host code the model cannot read
slides.notes: BrowserSessionClient resolves the clock and the browser through Reactor, and sends the authorize request through the Session transport: pap.browserJoin loads the form and submits it. A code from a message, a conversation or another page may come from someone else's browser, which would then join the user's Session; so the code comes only from the page the agent's own browser loaded.

slides.title: Join once, refuse the rest
slides.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Agent's browser
  participant A as Agent
  participant C as Company endpoint
  participant X as Another browser
  B->>C: GET the join page
  C-->>B: Form with code, join cookie
  A->>C: POST /authorize, code, Session header
  C-->>A: 204
  B->>C: POST the code, with cookie
  C->>C: Cookie, code authorized, not submitted
  C-->>B: 303 and Session cookie
  B->>C: Same code again
  C-->>B: 400, code already used
  X->>C: A fresh authorized code, no join cookie
  C-->>X: 400, and the code is used up
slides.notes: Follow the first submission. The company checks that the join cookie matches the code, and that the code was authorized in the agent's own request, is unexpired, and has not been submitted before. The first use goes through: 303 with the company's cookie. The same code again is refused: a code is used by the first request that submits it. A fresh code the agent authorized, submitted from another browser without the join cookie, is refused too, and is used up.

slides.title: The company's cookie
slides.statement: `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, set only on the join, and it **never outlives** the PAP Session.
slides.notes: The cookie acts for the account and scopes authorized in the agent's request, and stops acting for the account at sign-out. In the reference companies, the __Host-poppy_session cookie has no lifetime of its own, so signing out reaches the website on its next request. Joining again replaces it.

slides.title: What stays where

left.heading: Never in a URL or model context
items: The Session JWT and the access token

slides.notes: The code travels only in a request body, the Session JWT and the token only in the agent's own request. What the model gets back is the status of each step and yes-or-no evidence that each rule held.

slides.title: Run it yourself
slides.cta: The Pydantic AI example joins against the reference company, then replays a code and submits one from another browser, and sees both refused
slides.notes: The example runs Manzanita with its website on, in one process. It joins the agent's own browser through a Reactor pap.browserJoin contribution, checks the form carried the code alone, then tries a replayed code and a code from another browser. Upstream's Web browsing section has the rules in full.
